value: ARABELLA OBERLE, im Auftrag, LANDESARCHIV BERLIN, 29 September 2026, answering this archive's enquiry. Three scans attached and a page of instruction. "DIESE ANTWORT IST FÜR SIE KOSTENLOS" — this answer is free of charge.

STANDESAMT WEDDING, STERBEREGISTER, P Rep. 830 Nr. 114 — the death entry for GERTRUD LEIBHOLZ. Her own summary: "Sie starb am Morgen des 27. Februars, als Todesursache ist 'Selbstmord durch Zyankalivergiftung' angegeben. Sie starb im Jüdischen Krankenhaus, der Tod wurde durch den Polizeipräsidenten in Berlin gemeldet (Da bei einem unnatürlichen Tod die Polizei hinzugezogen wird, ist das nicht verwunderlich)."

STANDESAMT SCHÖNEBERG II, HEIRATSREGISTER, P Rep. 161 Nr. 171 — the LEIBHOLZ/LUWINSKI marriage of 5 January 1924, Nr. 6, with the divorce and the imposed-name note both flagged in her covering letter before this archive had read the margins.

field: *** WHAT SHE SENT THAT IS WORTH MORE THAN THE SCANS ***
value: *** THE SAMMELAKTE EXISTS AND THE 1923 AUFGEBOT PAPERS ARE IN IT. *** "In der zum Heiratsregister angelegten Sammelakte befinden sich keine Unterlagen zur Ehescheidung, es sind nur die AUFGEBOTSUNTERLAGEN AUS DEM JAHRE 1923 vorhanden. Die Sammelakte wurde noch nicht digitalisiert." A German banns file of 1923 normally contains THE BIRTH CERTIFICATES OF BOTH PARTIES — and a birth certificate names the parents. THE FOUR NAMES THE MARRIAGE ENTRY FAILED TO GIVE MAY BE SITTING IN A BOX IN BERLIN.

not digitised, so no scan; copies can be ordered for a fee through the Digitaler Antrag at service.berlin.de/dienstleistung/352800/. THIS IS A PURCHASE AND IT IS DAVID'S TO MAKE, NOT MINE. Drafted, not ordered.

field: and a clean negative on the divorce
value: THE SAMMELAKTE HOLDS NO DIVORCE PAPERS. The judgment is Landgericht Berlin 251. R. 80. 40 and it lives, if it lives, in a court record series and not in this file. Recorded so that nobody orders the Sammelakte expecting it.

field: *** WHAT SHE COULD NOT DO, AND WHY — THIS IS THE USEFUL FAILURE ***
value: KURT LUWINSKI'S BIRTH WAS NOT FOUND. "Leider reichen die von Ihnen gemachten Angaben nicht aus." The 1912 birth registers are NOT DIGITISED. To search the analogue registers she needs: full name (for women, the name at birth), the date of the event, and THE RESPONSIBLE STANDESAMT — "die bloße Angabe Berlin reicht nicht". THE LETTER THIS ARCHIVE SENT GAVE HER A NAME, A DATE AND THE WORD BERLIN.

field: and the reason is structural, not clerical
value: more than 150 Standesämter are held at the Landesarchiv AND THERE IS NO OVERARCHING NAME INDEX ACROSS THEM. Each office made its own Namensverzeichnisse, separately for births, marriages and deaths, and separately for every year. Without the office, there is nothing to open.

field: *** BUT SHE HANDED OVER THE METHOD ***
value: the Namensverzeichnisse ARE digitised even though the 1912 registers are not. Work out which Standesämter were active in 1912 from the Landesarchiv's own overview of its Standesamt holdings; search each one's digitised Namensverzeichnis for Kurt Luwinski; then order the register entry itself once he is found. THE SEARCH IS MINE TO DO AND IT IS NOT BLOCKED.

field: and a trap in her own system, given away for free
value: Bitte beachten Sie, dass das System leider Probleme mit dem Anzeigen von Umlauten hat. A Standesamt whose name carries an umlaut must be searched on the stem only — type "Neuk" and choose "Standesamt NeukÃ¶lln" from the list. THIS WOULD HAVE COST HOURS TO DISCOVER AND SHE WROTE IT DOWN UNASKED. It bears directly on SCHÖNEBERG, which is where this archive would start.

field: where this archive would actually start, and it is not Schöneberg
value: KURT WAS BORN 11 MAY 1912 AND THE LUWINSKI HOUSEHOLD WAS AT CHODOWIECKISTRASSE 32 IN THE 1913 DIRECTORY, compiled in the autumn of 1912. That is Prenzlauer Berg, which is STANDESAMT BERLIN VIII — not Schöneberg II, where this archive had already found a 1911-1913 birth index (P Rep. 161 Nr. 713) and where the family only demonstrably lived from January 1924. THE INDEX THE ARCHIVE HAD PICKED IS PROBABLY THE WRONG ONE, and the address it already holds names a better first candidate.
